body.x: The Seoul Business Agency (SBA, President and CEO Hyun Woo Kim) operated the Seoul Pavilion at CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and technology exhibition held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time), supporting the global market entry of a total of 69 Seoul-based startups.

Located in Eureka Park at the Venetian Expo, CES’s dedicated startup exhibition area, the Seoul Pavilion was designed as a strategic platform to showcase Seoul’s industrial competitiveness as a global metropolis on the world stage and to expand the city’s brand value into global markets.

In line with this objective, the Seoul Pavilion this year featured 69 startups across advanced technology fields such as AI, mobility, and healthcare, each presenting innovative solutions and introducing their capabilities to multinational visitors and investors.

A total of 19 organizations participated in the creation of the pavilion, including SBA, four district governments, five startup support organizations, and nine major universities. Even before the exhibition opened, the pavilion drew significant attention as 17 of the 69 participating startups were selected as CES Innovation Award winners, including one Best of Innovation award.

The CES Innovation Awards are presented by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), the event organizer, to products and technologies that demonstrate outstanding technological excellence, marketability, and design. In the global tech industry, the award is widely regarded as a key indicator of a company’s competitiveness.

With the goal of amplifying global attention on the Seoul Pavilion and its participating companies, SBA provided customized pre-exhibition consulting for approximately two months, strategically supporting startups in their pursuit of CES Innovation Awards. This meticulous and intensive support translated into tangible results, playing an important role in positioning Seoul as a city to watch in global technology competition.

On-site operations that emphasized collaboration and experience also stood out as a strength of the Seoul Pavilion. A total of 70 university student supporters, consisting of students from major Seoul universities and Korean students at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas (UNLV), were deployed on site. They supported booth operations and networking while gaining hands-on experience working alongside startups and growing with them.

By condensing Seoul’s startup ecosystem, where talent, institutions, and companies coexist and collaborate, the Seoul Pavilion went beyond being a simple exhibition space at CES 2026. It effectively functioned as a global business hub, laying a solid foundation for Seoul startups’ expansion into international markets.

At the center of this effort, Hyun Woo Kim, President and CEO of SBA, who led the creation of the Seoul Pavilion, spent the exhibition period visiting the site, encouraging startup achievements, and supporting connections with global investors, overseeing the pavilion’s overall operation. While tirelessly promoting Seoul’s innovation ecosystem, he appeared energized by the vibrant atmosphere created by the enthusiastic crowds at the pavilion.

Accordingly, AVING News conducted an interview with President Kim at the AVING Media Stage inside the Seoul Pavilion on the opening day of CES, January 6, to hear directly about the significance of this year’s pavilion, its positive outlook, and SBA’s goals at CES 2026.

body.x: Q1. AVING News: Since the opening day of CES 2026, you have been closely observing the operation of the Seoul Pavilion and the exhibition site as a whole. Could you share your first impressions?

A. Hyun Woo Kim, President and CEO of the Seoul Business Agency: CES has always been filled with crowds and energy, but this year the atmosphere feels different from previous years. One reason is that Chinese companies are noticeably less visible at Eureka Park, indicating a significant decline in China’s technological presence.

As a result, there is more open space on the exhibition floor than before, and the CTA’s treatment of Korean companies and institutions has also changed noticeably. I see it as a positive shift, especially as visitor attention toward the Seoul Pavilion has increased significantly.

Q2. AVING News: SBA, a core startup support organization that has led the growth of Seoul’s startup ecosystem, is again operating the Seoul Pavilion this year. Could you explain the meaning and intent behind the pavilion?

A. Hyun Woo Kim, President and CEO of the Seoul Business Agency: Among public institutions in Korea, I believe SBA is the one whose nature aligns most closely with this year’s CES theme, “Innovators Show Up.”

At CES, and especially at Eureka Park, many countries and institutions operate joint pavilions, but the Seoul Pavilion is clearly differentiated from others in both its internal and external composition and its planning intent.

We devoted significant effort to the exterior design to naturally draw visitors’ attention and spark interest in participating companies. Inside, the Seoul mascot “Haechi,” which was well received last year, actively engages visitors and encourages them to spend more time in the pavilion.

Internally, SBA is deeply committed to identifying trends through thorough research and continuous learning. The insights gained through this process have led to bold, creative initiatives by our staff, which, in turn, enhance both the effectiveness of company attraction strategies and the efficiency of on-site operations.

The media stage, introduced for the first time in the history of the Seoul Pavilion, also represents SBA’s creativity. By operating a space where stories from participating startups, overseas companies, and conference speakers—innovators attending CES—can be shared, we aimed to provide our companies with richer experiences and valuable assets.

body.x: Q3. AVING News: SBA has been recognized for its strong ability to leverage Seoul as a hub, based on the projects and achievements it has pursued so far.

A. Hyun Woo Kim, President and CEO of the Seoul Business Agency: Thanks to recognition of those efforts and results, SBA was honored with the 2025 National Brand Award in the Global City Brand Innovation Leadership category, alongside national athletes and entertainers. I believe the successful conclusion of “SeoulCon,” which drew strong interest from global fandoms and participants late last year, played a major role in that award.

To elaborate on the name SeoulCon, I felt strongly that it was time to create a sustainable foundation where the single keyword “Seoul” could elevate the brand value of both the city and Korea. Thinking back to how our parents’ generation would proudly say, “This cosmetic is from France,” to raise a product’s perceived value, the idea is similar.

Accordingly, SBA plans to actively allocate its budget to enhancing Seoul’s reputation so that the label “Made in Seoul” directly aligns with the brand value of Seoul-based companies and with positive perceptions of their products and services.
Q4. AVING News: The Global Innovation Forum, held in conjunction with CES 2026, appears to have been organized with a similar purpose.

A. Hyun Woo Kim, President and CEO of the Seoul Business Agency: That is correct. The Global Innovation Forum, held on the second day of CES 2026 (January 7), is a competitive pitching event featuring startups of various nationalities participating in CES.

Last year, it began under the name “Seoul Innovation Forum” through collaboration among startup support organizations from five countries. This year, the number of participating countries increased to 7, and the event was rebranded. Startups from each country present pitches on the products and technologies they showcased at CES 2026, and companies demonstrating excellence in technology and creativity receive prize money.

body.x: Q5. AVING News: SBA has built a reputation as a startup support organization that achieves remarkable results at CES each year. What are the strategies and keys behind this success?

A. Hyun Woo Kim, President and CEO of the Seoul Business Agency: Of the 69 companies participating in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 startups received CES Innovation Awards. Compared with the results of other startup support organizations, this is two to three times higher both in scale and in awards.

I believe this is the outcome of SBA’s full-cycle support, which goes beyond simply offering opportunities to participate in CES. We provide customized consulting for exhibition participation and Innovation Award challenges before the event, as well as post-exhibition strategy planning.

In particular, the know-how and data accumulated over the years of organizing the pavilion are extensive, and the benefits of these assets are well known among startups. As a result, demand to participate in the Seoul Pavilion continues to grow each year, and the pavilion’s competitiveness is further strengthened through careful selection of participating companies.
Q6. AVING News: Lastly, could you share a message of encouragement for the company representatives participating in the CES 2026 Seoul Pavilion?

A. Hyun Woo Kim, President and CEO of the Seoul Business Agency: The startups that earned their place in the Seoul Pavilion through rigorous screening and evaluation have each proven their competitiveness.

Rather than being swayed by immediate success or failure, I hope they maintain their confidence and persevere. Continuous innovation through technology and product development is important, but I believe the most critical factor in a startup’s success is the firm determination to endure and continue existing.
